title_zh: AndroidWorld：面向自主智能体的动态基准测试环境
one_line: Android benchmark of 116 parameterized tasks across 20 apps, rewarded by checkers reading system state via adb; zero-shot M3A/SeeAct online baselines, single run.
one_line_zh: 在20个真实安卓应用上构建116个参数化任务，用adb读取系统状态给出可执行奖励，并以M3A等零样本智能体做在线基线。

online_eval.quote: AndroidWorld provides reward signals primarily by managing application state using the Android Debug Bridge ( adb ), while also incorporating UI element validation where appropriate.

variance.quote: We set the seed to 30 and the temperature to 0 to aid reproducibility.

strong_baselines.quote: We implement SeeAct for the Android environment to evaluate how an existing model that performs well on web tasks ( Deng et al., 2023 ) can be adapted and applied to Android.

budget_matched.quote: Each task has a maximum allowed number of steps (detailed in Appendix F ), typically set to twice the number of steps needed by human annotators to complete the task.

cost_reported.quote: On average, M3A takes 3.9 minutes to complete a task, with the text-only version taking 2.5 minutes.

component_ablation.quote: The simplified agent variant M3A-Simple shows a significant performance drop on AndroidWorld tasks (19.8% vs 30.6% with GPT-4), indicating that additional prompting techniques and domain-specific guidance are beneficial

validator_check.quote: It is highly accurate because an application’s state can be quickly inspected and manipulated using the same mechanisms that the app itself utilizes.

code.quote: By releasing AndroidWorld and establishing benchmark performance with M3A , we aim to accelerate research and development in this area

evidence_level.quote: Table 3 presents the success rates (SR) for the agents and human performance on both task suites.

S1.quote: With adb , AndroidWorld has complete access to system resources including the file system, application databases, and system settings.

S2.quote: Using the underlying system state is much more durable than matching superficial UI changes.

S4.quote: Composite tasks are more challenging due to their complexity but provide partial rewards for subtask completion, aiding hill climbing.

F1.quote: It is highly accurate because an application’s state can be quickly inspected and manipulated using the same mechanisms that the app itself utilizes.

F2.quote: Each task has its own unique setup, reward determination logic, and teardown procedures (see Appendix D.2 and D.3 for more details), ensuring a fully reproducible suite of tasks.
